learning_outcomes:
Major
Programme:
Upon completion of the Programme,
Knowledge and Comprehension
Students
will have acquired the following knowledge:
(1)  |  Linear Algebra and Abstract
Algebra;
(2)  |  Analysis which includes
Calculus, Real Analysis, Complex Analysis, Fourier Analysis and Functional
Analysis;
(3)  |  Differential Geometry;
(4)  |  Computer programming for
Mathematics and Numerical Analysis;
(5)  |  Theoretical and practical
aspects of artificial intelligence.
Skills
and Generic Competencies
Students
will have acquired a set of generic competencies:
(1)  |  Ability to understand broad
mathematical literature independently;
(2)  |  Awareness of mathematical
problems arising in generic situations;
(3)  |  An ability to communicate
mathematical problems effectively;
(4)  |  Ability to formulate
mathematical problems and know how to find ways to solve them;
(5)  |  Ability to implement
AI/machine learning methods with modern computing tools;
(6)  |  Ability to evaluate AI/machine
learning models using appropriate metrics;
(7)  |  Ability
to solve real-life problems using mathematical software and AI/machine
learning.
Professional Skills
In addition, students will
have possessed professional skills in at least one of the following sectors:
(1)  |  Graduate school research;
(2)  |  Teaching;
(3)  |  Interdisciplinary research
between mathematics and other scientific disciplines.
Value and attitudes
Upon
graduation, our students will be able to apply their mathematical knowledge
generically in their future profession in a way that is unique for
mathematically trained experts. They will be able to make important original
contributions in mathematical sciences and lead breakthrough of
interdisciplinary mathematical-science applications.

Explanatory
Notes:
1.  |  Students
enrolled in the Mathematical Sciences and Artificial Intelligence Double Major Programme should normally spend four
regular terms at CUHK(SZ) during the four years of study, except
otherwise specified in 2. below.
2.  |  Students who join term-time exchange programme must
spend at least three regular terms at
CUHK(SZ) during the four years of study.
3.  |  Students
enrolled in the Mathematical Sciences and Artificial Intelligence Double
Major Programme can take substitute/equivalent/alternative courses of
University Core Requirements either at CUHK or CUHK(SZ). The list of
substitute/equivalent/alternative University Core Requirements courses is
available at this link (https://www.zsims.cuhk.edu.hk/en/).
Students should not take a course and its
substitute/equivalent/alternative course. Should they do so, only one
course will be counted towards the fulfillment of the unit requirements.
Grades of relevant substitute/equivalent/alternative courses taken at
CUHK(SZ) will be transferred to CUHK for the purpose of calculation of
GPA, Major GPA and credit units.
4.  |  All Faculty Package, courses at
2000 or above level in the requirements of the 1st Major Programme, as
well as those labeled as #, and the Research Component/Capstone
Course/Final Year Project, will be included in the calculation of Major
GPA for honours classification.
5.  |  Courses taken to fulfill the
requirements of the 1st Major cannot be counted towards the fulfillment
of requirements of the 2nd Major, and vice versa.
6.  |  A student who wishes to
transfer to the programmes offered by the Faculty of Science or Faculty
of Engineering shall follow the prevailing rules and regulations of the
University and obtain prior permission from the School Director through
written application. Such applications should be made one month before
the commencement of the University’s designated application period for
change of programme. No such application shall be accepted once the
application period as announced by the University has commenced. In
general, students must apply for a change of programme no later than the
third year of attendance of their undergraduate studies.
7.  |  Students admitted by
CUHK will be conferred a Bachelor of Science degree in Mathematical
Sciences and Artificial Intelligence upon completion of all graduation
requirements. Students may apply to pursue Ph.D. study under the
arrangements of the Articulated B.Sc.–Ph.D.
Programme (ABP) in Mathematical Sciences, and they must declare the
opt-in according to the stipulated procedures by the beginning of the
fourth year of attendance. Students are required to obtain a Bachelor of
Science degree with honours not lower than Second Class and to satisfy the minimum admission requirements prescribed by
the Graduate School and Zhizhen School in order to be eligible to proceed
with postgraduate studies, subject to the prevailing University
regulations and approval by the relevant authorities. Graduates from the
Bachelor’s programmes from CUHK are deemed to have fulfilled the
University’s English Language requirements.
8.  |  Students
who wish to pursue Ph.D. study under the ABP should take note of the
following:
(i)  |  For CUHK students who
are subsequently admitted to the Ph.D. of the ABP, the 5000-level courses
that they complete under this programme will be automatically recognized
to fulfill the coursework requirement for the Ph.D. Programme, subject to
prevailing guidelines. No application for course and unit
exemptions is required.
(ii)  |  In
order to fulfill the graduation requirements for the postgraduate study,
students must complete a minimum of 9 months of non-local
learning/research experience, with at least 3 consecutive months of such
experience. A formal term-time exchange programme during undergraduate
study, or non-consecutive and substantial non-local learning/research
experiences of 4 months or more offered by the University, Colleges, the
Faculty of Engineering or Science, Zhizhen School, the Mathematics
Department and other relevant programmes may also be considered, subject
to the approval of the Division Head.
